name: Zero Width Need Not Give a Low-Width Common-Section Prefix
statement: There is a 579-concept dismantlable ample class $C$ on 25 coordinates with nonnested sections and intersection $H$ a coordinate edge such that $\sigma(C)=0<\min\{\sigma(C_0;H),\sigma(C_1;H)\}$.
proof: Build the two sections from disjoint copies of the rooted 289-vertex ample factor $R$: one section is $A=\{(r,0):r\in R\}$ and the other is $B=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(e,r):r\in R\}$, meeting in $H=\{(0,0),(e,0)\}$. A block order using a zero-width order of the upper copy, then a zero-width order of the lower copy starting at $e$, then the final common vertex has width zero. The retained-edge obstruction in $R$ makes $\sigma(A;H)>0$. Conditioning the active coordinate of $e$ maps $(B,H)$ to $(R,\{0\})$, whose prescribed width is positive, and paired-minor monotonicity gives the other inequality.
comments: The construction makes no minimum-cardinality claim. It limits common-section-first upper bounds but does not refute zero-width preservation under two-sided dismantlable tests.
